newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares ends lower,reversing Thursday trend.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares ends lower,reversing Thursday trend.

text.p: Italian shares closed lower on Friday in a sharp correction to rises seen on Thursday. A partial recovery on a surprise fall in U.S. non-farm payrolls did not last long and the market failed to be excited by Wall Street's solid gains, traders said.

The fall in September Italian mutual fund inflows announced earlier today and the sharp outflow from equity funds confirmed the move of investors away from the stock market and into bonds which have been soaring in recent sessions, one dealer said.
The All-share Mibtel index was down 2.05 percent at 10,087 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed at 2.43 percent at 15,160.

State energy giant Eni saw continued selling ahead of a market placement of a second tranche of its shares later this month on investor hopes of being able to buy at a cheaper price. It ended 3.02 percent down at 7,302 lire.

Olivetti rose from the opening as investors digested news the group aimed for divestments, including that of its troubled PC business, this year and next to raise up to 1.2 trillion lire. The stock closed 4.33 percent at 540.1 lire.
But some London analysts at a meeting with CEO Roberto Colaninni today expressed doubts. "They have it all to do, it's very much wait and see at the moment," said one.
Tyre and cable maker Pirelli was a gainer against the trend, up 0.54 percent at 2,817 lire after a presentation pleased analysts.
Fiat was 0.93 percent off at 4,240 and telecoms all lost with mobile phone operator TIM down 2.02 percent at 3,341.

Financial holding company Gemina shares were suspended shortly before the opening pending an extraordinary board meeting to be followed by a statement. The company said the baord would not be discussing acquisitions, but one broker said there was talk of divestments in view of future purchases.
